body.statement: Along the retained even tail \(n\ge N_0\), does the actual-filtration characteristic handle establish, for every fixed \(L,R<\infty\), uniformly over integers \(0\le m<\min\{\lfloor nL\rfloor,T_n\}\) with \(\|Z_n(W_{n,m})\|\le R\), that \(n\,\mathbb E(\Delta Z_{n,m}\mid\mathcal F_{n,m})+4Z_n(W_{n,m})+8\gamma(D_n(W_{n,m})^{\mathsf T},0)^{\mathsf T}/\|D_n(W_{n,m})\|^2\to0\) in probability, \(n\,\mathbb E(\Delta Z_{n,m}\Delta Z_{n,m}^{\mathsf T}\mid\mathcal F_{n,m})\to8I_{k+1}\) in probability, and the conditional jump Lindeberg remainder tends to zero, without empirical-law convergence, projected Markovianity, stabilization, or outcome-residual independence; and can the terminal crossing be transferred separately from its exact transposition increment and vanishing jump size, without using \(D/\|D\|^2\) at or after \(T_n\)?
body.justification: This is the first nonroutine proof boundary: the projected scores are generally non-Markov and the Metropolis kink can create an order-one residual drift at arbitrary balanced states.
body.gap: Roberts, Gelman, and Gilks control Metropolis characteristics for high-dimensional product targets; no located theorem provides these actual-path finite-population exchange bounds for original PSRR.
body.consumer: An affirmative answer supplies pre-entry predictable characteristics and a separate terminal-crossing argument for compact containment, martingale-problem identification, and continuous first-hit transfer.
